# RM3 imported-spectrum MCR histories

The three `spectrumData*.mat` files are byte-identical to the published
Applications inputs at pinned commit
`d53d4d4c9eda2581f04204f5d394a6ef84bb099e` (Git blob IDs
`3754a363b8a5d33a8cd5afee722849277fd74766`,
`edc93f5c0f8124f54b621818d3c1f18615f2da1f`, and
`bbd569768964b1c3685258d3f221483919db05f9`). They contain each
case's spectrum and saved wave phases; Python does not receive source body
motion or forces.

`source.npz` selects float64 columns without rounding from the successful
[pinned R2025b MATLAB reference-model sweep](https://github.com/cmudrc/wec-sim-python/actions/runs/38282150325), using WEC-Sim core
`0753b2e47f2457c078751dcfe5d251d1767b80ab`. The complete CSVs remain
in that run's `matlab-RM3_MCR_SEASTATE-baseline` artifact. The NPZ SHA-256 is
`501145af44398328287f1e3d2fd15a8b0ee3c8e84c22f5f04685279dbaa8f6d7`.

`summary` contains the three original signed mean PTO powers. Each
`case1`–`case3` array has 4,001 rows and these 18 columns:

| Columns | MATLAB source |
| --- | --- |
| 0–1 | Time and wave elevation |
| 2–7 | Float surge/heave/pitch position, then velocity |
| 8–13 | Spar surge/heave/pitch position, then velocity |
| 14–17 | PTO stroke, speed, axial force, signed mechanical power |

The public `WEC.floating_joint` regression reads the MAT spectrum and
independently advances both bodies and the PTO for each 400 s case. It uses
the explicit `simulink_delay` added-mass timing for numerical comparison;
the implicit physical default remains unchanged. The default's PTO power is
nonnegative for every sample, and its 400 s PTO work differs from source by
0.891%, 0.763%, and 0.671% across the three seas, below a separate 1% gate.
Its body surge can differ by 0.268 m, so the default work gate does not claim
published-motion parity. These are stronger public API gates for three already
counted published inputs, not new case badges.

A fresh local R2025b Update 7 run with the pinned core and Applications commits
also passed the direct-source gates in `test_rm3_mcr_seastate_parity.py` using
HDF5 regenerated by the pinned `bemio.m`. Its selected body samples differ
from this archive by at most `5.8e-13` in their units, PTO samples by
`3.1e-9`, and wave samples exactly. The bundled RM3 HDF5 has slightly different
displacement volumes; rerunning the public source-delay case with the freshly
generated HDF5 changes body position by at most `3.92e-5` m across the seas.
